$comment: Figure manifest. A figure is an ARTEFACT, so it carries the same contract as a usage figure: what it shows, what produced it, and when. The data files beside this manifest are REAL OUTPUT of the programs the page is about — nothing here is drawn to look plausible.
rule: DESIGN.md binds colour to the image layer: hue band 70-145 degrees, at most four series, each at least 3:1 against its ground. Where a dataset has more series than that, the surplus is drawn as an ink-tertiary family and the series that carry the argument keep the colour. That is a resolution, not an exception.

figures.alt: A measured spectrum with a four-component pseudo-Voigt fit, and the residual beneath it.
figures.caption: Four overlapping pseudo-Voigt components resolved from one measured band. The residual strip underneath is the part the model does not explain — it is shown because a fit without it is a picture, not a result.

figures.alt: Tanabe-Sugano diagram for a d5 configuration, showing the sextet ground term crossed by a doublet at high field.
figures.caption: d⁵ term energies against field strength. Every excited term is a quartet or a doublet above a sextet ground state, so every d–d transition here is spin-forbidden — which is why manganese(II) salts are almost colourless. The two highlighted terms are the pair that swaps at the spin crossover.
figures.source: TanabeSugano 2.0.0 · d5, B=860 cm⁻¹, C=3850 cm⁻¹ · MIT, Anselm Hahn

placementRule: Where a figure appears is content, not layout, so it is declared here. 'lead' puts it inside the lead case study; 'motivation' under the opening prose; 'category:<id>' inside that project sheet.
